title: Hydration-Induced beta-Sheet Crosslinking of alpha-Helical-Rich Spider Prey-Wrapping Silk

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Molecular-level structure of native aciniform (prey-wrapping) silk after conversion to insoluble fibre is barely understood. Contact with water drives fusion and crosslinking of neighbouring wrapping-silk fibres through a change in protein secondary structure.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: Water raises beta-sheet content in silkworm fibres and silk films, but within a single fibre, not between strands

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Water-soaked fibres fuse into larger fibres and continuous fibrous sheets/mats with collapsed inter-fibre space. Water soaking raises Ala beta-sheet content at the expense of random-coil structure (about 30% to 41%).
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (STR/microstructure/shape), n9 (STR/chemistry/bonding), n10 (STR/chemistry/bonding), n11 (STR/microstructure/feature_size). Premises: Spin-diffusion model relating WISE build-up time tau_m* to rigid-domain size

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Water plasticises disordered linker and loosely coiled helix regions, which convert to small intermolecular beta-sheets bridging chains of adjacent fibres
states.detail: Absorbed: n12 (MEC/pathway). Premises: W-subunit solution structure: helix 1 holds 11 of the 26 Ala, the linker 5

states.title: Performance state
states.head: On wrapped prey during extra-oral digestion the wrapping silk fuses into fibrous bundles and mats

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Prey-wrapping silk crosslinks between fibres on wetting, driven by beta-sheet formation from disordered and loose helical motifs while coiled-coils stay intact

nodes.note: native-to-soaked change is moderate (C-beta beta-sheet still below the 17 ppm helix peak); wet-sheared C-beta beta-sheet nearly equals the helix peak; scaling on Gly C-alpha is stated in text only Val fits (right) keep a similar alpha-helix component across treatments; native Ala fit carries the asterisked contamination spike the same spike appears in the native F4c fit; the native beta-sheet baseline depends on excluding it; '*' is not among the OCR annotation strings

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: Linear build-up meets the plateau at tau_m^1/2 about 5.0 (AC) and 6.7 (MA) ms^1/2. Squared, the F5c crossings give tau_m* about 25 ms (AC) and 45 ms (MA), not the 4.5 and 6.6 ms quoted; text values fit a ms^1/2 reading
nodes.solves: Water-inaccessible beta-sheet domains in hydrated, crosslinked AC silk are small, about 4-6 nm
nodes.op: compare across conditions, convert to quantity, cross check consistency, read characteristic point
nodes.note: arrows in panel c; about 5 points in the AC rising region, error bars overlap unit mismatch (ms vs ms^1/2) and AC 4.5 vs ~5.0 bear on the 4-6 nm domain size
